name: State of Israel

places.name: Bar Lev Line (Suez Canal east bank)

areaKm2.note: Pre-1967 lines 20,770 km2 (mid; the hb:1960 polygon). Held since 1967 with no separate basemap polygon: Sinai ~61,000, Golan ~1,150, West Bank ~5,600, Gaza ~360 km2 -> ~89,000 km2 controlled (high).

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1973 = 3,278k (mid); World Bank 1973 male+female = 3,278,000; OWID/HYDE 3,163,042 (low). Israeli citizens within its own jurisdiction incl. East Jerusalem; the ~1M Palestinians of the occupied West Bank and Gaza are excluded.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) urban share 1973 = 62.2% (low). Israel CBS national definition ~85% in the early 1970s (high); mid between. Grade C.

activePersonnel.note: Standing force = conscripts + career regulars before mobilisation (6 Oct 1973, Yom Kippur). COW NMC v7 milper 1973 = 130,000 is a year average including October mobilisation (high). IISS Military Balance 1973-74 order of magnitude ~115,000 regulars incl. conscripts (not fetched; edition paywalled). Grade C.

trainedReserves.note: Reservists, mobilised from the morning of 6 Oct (Golan reinforced 9 h after the war began). Total strength 375,000 (Rabinovich 2004 p. 54) to 415,000 per the Yom Kippur War infobox, minus ~115,000-130,000 standing -> ~245,000-300,000 reservists.

supportPersonnel.note: Air force (~17,000), navy (~5,000), armour, artillery, engineer, signals, logistics and staff inside the ~115,000 standing force; remainder after the P roles. Reconstruction, grade C.

mobilizationRatio.note: 375,000-415,000 under arms (Yom Kippur War infobox) / 3.28M population = 11.4-12.7% achieved; ceiling ~16%.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Standing infantry only: Golani brigade, Nahal, conscript infantry battalions and the reserve-brigade garrison of the Bar Lev Line (~450 men in 16 strongpoints on 6 Oct). Reserve infantry brigades enter via trainedReserves. Reconstruction, grade C.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Galil not yet issued, FN FAL/Uzi; few ATGMs, infantry neglected in favour of armour.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: well trained, but doctrine of "all-tank" armour neglected infantry-armour cooperation (Pollack, Arabs at War ch. on 1973).

count.note: Educated guess: paratroop brigade (35th) conscript battalions plus Sayeret reconnaissance units.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: light-infantry kit, M72 LAW.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: elite volunteer units (Chinese Farm, Hermon recapture).

count.note: Yom Kippur War infobox: 945 artillery units of 100 mm and up. Low = pieces with the regular army only (~60%).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: M109 and M107 SP guns arriving; still many Sherman-based conversions.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: artillery a weak arm; IDF relied on the air force for fire support.

count.note: Yom Kippur War infobox: 1,700 tanks (Sunday Times Insight Team pp. 372-373). High ~2,100 allows estimates incl. Shermans in storage and captured T-54/55 (Tiran). Centurion (Sho't), M48/M60 (Magach), Super Sherman, Tiran.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: 105 mm-gunned Sho't and Magach equal to or better than T-55/T-62; no ATGM-resistant armour.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: superior gunnery (7th Brigade at the Valley of Tears) but costly unsupported tank charges on 8 Oct.

count.note: Yom Kippur War infobox: 3,000 armored carriers (M3 half-tracks, M113 entering service).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: mostly WWII half-tracks.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: mechanised infantry underused tactically.

count.note: Split of 440 combat aircraft (Yom Kippur War infobox): F-4E Phantom ~125-130 (multirole, counted here) plus Mirage IIIC/Nesher ~100-110. Grade C for the split.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: F-4E among the best fighters of 1973; Mirage/Nesher dominant in dogfights.

training.note: Rubric row: training 1.0. Evidence: air-to-air kill ratios of the order of 20:1 or better over the Arab air forces.

count.note: Rest of the 440 (Yom Kippur War infobox): A-4 Skyhawk ~160-170 plus IAI Sa'ar/Super Mystere ~25-30. Official losses 102 aircraft incl. 53 A-4 (Israeli Air Force article).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: A-4 subsonic, little ECM against SA-6.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: high skill, but Operation Model 5 lost 6 Phantoms for 1 SAM battery.

count.note: Educated guess: CH-53, Super Frelon, Bell 205, Bell 206 and Alouette III; no fetched order of battle.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: modern transport helicopters, no attack helicopters yet.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: Mount Hermon heliborne assault 21-22 Oct.

count.note: Educated guess: Israel had retired its destroyers by 1973 (Eilat sunk 1967, Yafo decommissioned); the fleet was built around missile boats.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: no modern major combatant.

count.note: 12 Sa'ar 2/3 plus 2 Sa'ar 4 missile boats (6 at the Battle of Baltim: 2 Sa'ar 4, 2 Sa'ar 3, 1 Sa'ar 2, 1 Sa'ar 1) plus larger patrol craft; high counts Dabur patrol boats. Grade C.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Gabriel missiles plus ECM and chaff defeated every Styx fired (Latakia, Baltim).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: first missile-boat battles won without loss.

count.note: Educated guess: S/T-class boats Tanin, Rahav, Leviathan after the 1968 loss of INS Dakar; Gal class not before 1976.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: WWII-era boats.

count.note: Educated guess: Jericho I ballistic missiles reportedly operational in small numbers by 1973; launcher count unpublished.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: ~500 km road-mobile missile.

count.note: Educated guess: MIM-23 Hawk batteries (several battalions after 1970 US deliveries; one hit at Ophir on 6 Oct, Yom Kippur War article) plus 40 mm and Vulcan AAA batteries.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Improved Hawk-era SAMs.

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: strategic surprise from the "conception" failure (Agranat Commission), poor 8 Oct counterattack; then recovery, canal crossing and encirclement of the Third Army.

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75. Evidence: reserve units mobilised and fought within hours; Golan brigades held while outnumbered.

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75-1.0. Evidence: initial overconfidence and shock, but existential defence of the Golan and Sinai.

weapons.note: Anchor: between 8 (1943) and 9 (1985). Evidence: Gabriel anti-ship missiles, TOW and Maverick arriving by US airlift, Shrike ARMs; few ATGMs at the start.

armor.note: Anchor: 8 = RHA, 9 = composite. Evidence: M60/Centurion steel armour, no composite.

ships.note: Anchor: 8 = radar, 9 = Aegis/nuclear subs. Evidence: Sa'ar missile boats with Gabriel and electronic warfare suites.

fortification.note: Anchor: 8 = concrete lines. Evidence: Bar Lev Line strongpoints behind a sand rampart; Golan anti-tank ditch.

logistics.note: Anchor: 8 motor transport, 9 airlift. Evidence: motorised; dependent on the US Operation Nickel Grass airlift for resupply.

communications.note: Anchor: 8 company radio, 9 satellite comms. Evidence: VHF radio to tank level; no satellite comms.

isr.note: Anchor: 8 = radar, 9 = satellites. Evidence: Hermon SIGINT site, Firebee reconnaissance drones, US satellite data late in the war; strategic warning failed.

air.note: Anchor: air 9 = 1985. Evidence: F-4E with radar-guided AAMs and ECM pods; A-4 Skyhawk subsonic. audit 2026-10-30: mid 8.8 -> 8.71, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for 1973 (8.714); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

cyber.note: No military computer-network capability before ~1985 (cyber anchor 9 = 1990 networks).

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID CSV): Israel 1973 = 15,374 (2011 int$). Range +/-10%.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via OWID: 1972 = 20.4% (last peacetime, low), 1973 = 27.9% (mid and high, war year).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: industry about a third of output; World Bank NV.IND.TOTL.ZS has no Israel value for 1973.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of the labour force (share of food output not eaten by the farm population; no calorie self-sufficiency adjustment). World Bank WDI Database Archives (version 1999 Apr), SL.AGR.TOTL.ZS "Labor force in agriculture (% of total)" (ILO-based) Israel 1973 = 8.5%. Share 8.5% (range 7.0-10.0%) -> 0.915 (0.9-0.93).

annualCohort.note: World Bank SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y and SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN (https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/ISR;EGY/indicator/SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y?date=1967:1973&format=json): 1,634,642 x 10.12% / 5 = ~33,100 males per year. Women were also conscripted (1,643,358 x 9.68% / 5 = ~31,800 more a year); they are left out so the field compares across nations. audit 2026-10-30: males only, the conscript-pool convention of all other snapshots (derived:cohort-from-agegroup applied to the male term only); was 64,900 for both sexes.

artillery.note: Educated guess: Soltam mortars and SP conversions.

armor.note: Educated guess: no domestic new-build tanks (Merkava from 1979); rebuilds of Centurions and captured T-54/55.

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess: IAI Nesher (Mirage 5 copy) production 1971-74, ~60 built in total.

ships_minor.note: Educated guess: Sa'ar 4 missile boats built at Haifa from 1973.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: paved roads within pre-1967 Israel plus the military Lateral and Artillery roads in Sinai.

railKm.note: Educated guess: Israel Railways ~780 km; no rail into Sinai.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: Haifa, Ashdod, Eilat, plus Sharm el-Sheikh used as a naval base.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: ZIM and tanker fleet of the early 1970s, roughly 2-2.5M GRT x 1.5.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: operations on the Suez front ~250-300 km from Negev bases via Refidim; west-bank pocket 100 km from Cairo.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS estimate via OWID: Israel 1973 = 15 (undeclared; reported nuclear alert in October 1973). Range +/- 5.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: familiar terrain, fortified lines (Bar Lev, Golan ditch) and full population support; the occupied Sinai gives depth but is not home ground.

notes: Snapshot date 6 October 1973 (Egyptian-Syrian surprise attack on Yom Kippur). Territory: hb:1960:Israel is the pre-1967 polygon; Sinai, Golan, West Bank and Gaza were occupied but have no separate basemap polygon (areaKm2 high counts them). Population excludes the Palestinians of the occupied territories. Personnel convention: activePersonnel = conscripts + career regulars (~115,000); trainedReserves = reservists mobilised from 6 Oct (~275,000). P roles hold standing infantry only. Key sources: Yom Kippur War infobox (1,700 tanks, 3,000 APCs, 945 guns, 440 aircraft; Rabinovich, Sunday Times Insight), Israeli Air Force and Battle of Baltim articles, COW NMC v7, SIPRI via OWID, Maddison 2023. IISS Military Balance 1973-74 and Dupuy, Elusive Victory could not be fetched; activePersonnel mid relies on recalled IISS order of magnitude (grade C). US airlift (Operation Nickel Grass, from 14 Oct) replaced losses and is not in the snapshot.
